title: Tarkovsky's Stalker and The Brothers Karamazov by Fyodor Dostoevsky

commenti.body:
I like that novel and that movie but the only influence seems perhaps of tone, not of character, etc.  You cherry pick a few similarities between the two works and ignore obvious and deep differences.  Procrustes.

>I believe the stalker, writer, and professor are modeled on

No, Tarkovsky is clear in his book and interviews he doesn't do symbolism.

He is clear in his book and interviews he avoids symbolism whenever he can.

He is clear in his book and interviews he doesn't model *this* on *that*.

He is clear in his book and interviews he doesn't want viewers to interpret his movies but to feel emotions or at most to be aware of spiritual things, not to think of secular stuff like literary allusions.  But you and I are free to think as we please.

I like your concept. But can I have a little bit of a fight.

There were 4 brothers Karamazov.

Dmitry Karamazov, he has a passionate, impetuous, explosive character. A writer, he's still different.

Dostoevsky uses Smerdyakov to see Ivan's ideas to their logical conclusions. Since Stalker is literally a journey into the soul Tarkovsky didn't need a character equivalent to refute atheism and scientism. 

Of all three characters in Stalker, the writer is the most explosive. He is the first to wallow in despair in front of the room and his monologue after encountering the zone's trap mirrors Dmitri's self pity. The fact he's an artist does alter the dynamic a bit, but I still see Dmitri in his character.
